variantrule.name: Boost
entries: You can attempt to boost a function of your ship. Each function can only be boosted once on each of the ship's turns, and each time you try to boost a function of the ship after the first, the DC increases by 5, cumulatively, until the start of your next turn.

entries.name: Boost Engines
entries: You can attempt to boost your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}. When you take the Boost Engines action, you make a DC 10 Strength ({@skill Boost|sw5e-sotg}) check. On a success you increase your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} by 50 until the end of your ship's next turn.

entries.name: Boost Shields
entries: You can attempt to boost your shields. When you take the Boost Shields action, you make a DC 10 Strength ({@skill Boost|sw5e-sotg}) check. On a success, you roll a shield die, without expending it, and gain temporary shield points equal to the result that last until the start of your ship's next turn.

entries.name: Boost Weapons
entries: You can attempt to boost your weapon output. When you take the Boost Weapons action, the next time this turn your ship would deal damage, you make a DC 10 Strength ({@skill Boost|sw5e-sotg}) check. On a success, you have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the damage roll.

variantrule.name: Cover
entries: Asteroids, ships, debris, and other obstacles can provide cover during starship combat, making a target more difficult to harm. A target can benefit from cover only when an attack or other effect originates on the opposite side of the cover.
There are four degrees of cover. If a target is behind multiple sources of cover, only the most protective degree applies; the degrees aren't added together.

A target with {@b one-quarter cover} has a +2 bonus to AC and Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}. A target has one-quarter cover if an obstacle blocks at least one-fourth of it.
A target with {@b half cover} has a +3 bonus to AC and Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}. A target has half cover if an obstacle blocks at least half of it.

A target with {@b three-quarters cover} has a +5 bonus to AC and Dexterity {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}. A target has three-quarters cover if about three-quarters of it is covered by an obstacle.

A target with {@b total cover} can't be targeted directly by an attack or a power, although some powers can reach such a target by including it in an area of effect. A target has total cover if it is completely concealed by an obstacle.

variantrule.name: Destruction Saving Throw
entries: At the start of the ship's turn, if the ship has 0 hull points, you must make a special saving throw, called a destruction saving throw, to determine whether you can salvage your ship. Unlike other {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throws}, this one isn't tied to any ability score. Roll a {@dice d20}. If the roll is 10 or higher, you succeed. Otherwise, you fail. A success has no effect by itself; on your third success, your ship becomes stable. On a failure, your ship suffers 1 level of {@condition System Damage|sw5e-sotg|system damage}.

{@b {@i Rolling 1 or 20.}} When you make a destruction saving throw and roll a 1 on the {@dice d20}, it counts as two failures, causing 2 levels of {@condition System Damage|sw5e-sotg|system damage}. If you roll a 20 on the {@dice d20}, your ship regains 1 hull point.

{@b {@i Damage at 0 Hull Points.}} If your ship takes any damage while it has 0 hull points, it suffers 1 level of {@condition System Damage|sw5e-sotg|system damage}. If the damage is from a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit}, it suffers 2 levels instead. If the damage equals or exceeds its hull point maximum, it is instantly destroyed.

variantrule.name: Detect
entries: When you take this action, you devote your attention to finding something. Depending on the nature of your detection, the DM might have you make a Wisdom ({@skill Scan|sw5e-sotg}) check or an Intelligence ({@skill Probe|sw5e-sotg}) check.

variantrule.name: Direct
entries: When you take this action, the creature gains {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the next {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} it makes to perform the task you are helping with, provided that it makes the check before the start of your next turn. Alternatively, you can direct a friendly creature that can hear you in attacking another target. If your ally attacks the target before the start of your next turn, the first {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} is made with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}. This action can be taken multiple times on a ship's turn.

variantrule.name: Fire
entries: The most common action to take in combat is This action. With this action, you can make an attack (or attacks) with one ship weapon. This action may be taken multiple times on a ship's turn, but normally only once per weapon. A crewmember firing from the helm has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack rolls} with primary and secondary weapons.

variantrule.name: Firing Arc
entries: Ships have a firing arc, which is determined by the hardpoint on which they are mounted. Fixed hardpoints offer a limited firing arc, while turret hardpoints add an unlimited firing arc.

entries.name: Limited Firing Arc
entries: Many weapons can only fire in a single direction, indicated by a limited firing arc. The available arcs are spaced 90 degrees from each other and consist of: forward, aft, port, and starboard.
Weapons with a limited firing arc only fire at targets within a 90-degree arc, with the ship's center point as the arc's vertex.

entries.name: Unlimited Firing Arc
entries: Weapons with an unlimited firing arc can fire at any target within range and line of sight.

variantrule.name: Harass
entries: When you take the Harass action, make an opposed Dexterity ({@skill Maneuvering|sw5e-sotg}) check against a target within one size category of you and within normal range of at least one forward-facing primary weapon. That weapon cannot be fired this turn.

On a success, if the target voluntarily leaves its space before the start of your next turn, it takes damage as though it suffered a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} with the harassing weapon.

variantrule.name: Helm
entries: When you take this action, you choose from the following options. Only one Helm action can be taken per turn.

entries.name: Attack Run
entries: When you move at least 150 feet towards a target, you may declare an Attack Run. You must have a clear path towards your target, and nothing should hinder your path (such as {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|sw5e-phb|difficult terrain} or obstacles). If you finish this movement within range of your target, you may follow it with one of these options: {@b Fire.} You may make a ship {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} from a forward-facing limited arc without suffering the normal {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}. If you attack with a tertiary or quaternary weapon, the attack deals additional damage equal to the distance of your attack run divided by 50, up to your ship's Strength modifier (minimum of 1).

{@b Ram.} You may make a Ram attempt with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on your Strength ({@skill Ram|sw5e-sotg}) check. If you succeed, the target ship takes additional damage equal to the distance of your Attack Run divided by 50, up to your ship's Constitution modifier (minimum of +1).

entries.name: Conceal
entries: When you take the Conceal action, you make a Dexterity ({@skill Hide|sw5e-sotg}) check in an attempt to hide your ship, following the rules in chapter 7 for hiding.

entries.name: Dogfight
entries: When you engage a single enemy, you duck and weave, vying for a good shot while avoiding theirs. You choose a target and make an opposed Dexterity ({@skill Maneuvering|sw5e-sotg}) check. On a success, you cause the next attack made against your ship by the target to suffer from {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}, but you grant the next attack made against your ship by a different target {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}. Additionally, you can perform a primary or tertiary {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|weapon attack} from a forward-facing limited firing arc against that ship without suffering the normal {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}.

entries.name: Evade
entries: When you take the Evade action, you focus entirely on avoiding attacks. Until the start of your next turn, any attack roll made against you has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} if you can see the attacker on your instruments, and you make Dexterity saving throws with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}.

This action affects your entire ship: any {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} or attack made by your ship or anyone on it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} until the end of your ship's next turn. The effects of Evade end if you are {@condition Incapacitated|sw5e-phb} or if your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed} drops to 0.

entries.name: Fly
entries: When you take the Fly action, you gain extra movement for the current turn. The increase equals your {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}, after applying any modifiers.

This action affects your ship's ability to stay on target: any {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} or attack made by your ship or anyone on it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} until the end of your ship's next turn.

entries.name: Harass
entries: When you take the Harass action, make an opposed Dexterity ({@skill Maneuvering|sw5e-sotg}) check against a target within one size category of you and within normal range of at least one of your forward-facing primary weapons. This weapon cannot be fired this turn. On a success, if the target voluntarily leaves its square before the beginning of your next turn, it takes damage as though it suffered a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit} with the primary weapon used to harass.

entries.name: Hard Turn
entries: When you take the Hard Turn action, you turn your ship 90 degrees without expending any of your flying {@variantrule Speed|sw5e-phb|speed}.

entries.name: Ram
entries: When you take the Ram action, you make a Strength ({@skill Ram|sw5e-sotg}) check opposed by the target's Dexterity ({@skill Maneuvering|sw5e-sotg}) check. On a failed check the ram fails. On a success, both you and the target ship take kinetic damage equal to two of your ship's Hull Dice + your ship's Strength modifier. If your ship has shield points remaining, your ship instead takes half this damage.

variantrule.name: Hull Points
entries: Hull points represent a ship's hull integrity. A ship's current hull points can be any number from its hull point maximum down to 0.
Whenever a ship takes damage, that damage is subtracted from its hull points. The loss of hull points has no effect on a ship's capabilities until the ship drops to 0 hull points.
At tier 0, hull points are determined by Hull Dice and the ship's Constitution modifier. Record hull point maximum, Hull Die type, and Hull Die count on the starship sheet.
Damage to hulls is permanent until repaired. When a ship receives repairs, hull points regained are added to its current hull points and can't exceed its hull point maximum.

variantrule.name: Interfere
entries: When you take this action, you make a Charisma ({@skill Interfere|sw5e-sotg}) check contested by the target's Wisdom ({@skill Scan|sw5e-sotg}) check. If you succeed, the subject has {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on the next {@variantrule Ability Check|sw5e-phb|ability check} or {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} it makes before the start of your next turn. This action can be taken multiple times on a ship's turn.

variantrule.name: Making an Attack
entries: Whether you're firing laser cannons or a railgun, a starship attack follows these steps:
{@b 1. Choose a target.} Pick a target within your attack's range.
{@b 2. Determine modifiers.} The GM determines {@variantrule Cover|sw5e-sotg|cover}, {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage}, and {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage}.
{@b 3. Resolve the attack.} Make an {@variantrule Attack Roll|sw5e-phb|attack roll} or, for some weapons, a {@variantrule Saving Throw|sw5e-phb|saving throw}; on a hit, roll damage.

entries.name: Attack Rolls
entries: Roll {@dice d20} + your {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} (if you have at least one deployment rank) + the ship's Wisdom modifier + weapon bonuses. The attack hits if the total meets or exceeds the target's {@variantrule Armor Class|sw5e-phb|AC}. Ships are proficient with properly installed weapons.
A natural 20 is a {@variantrule Critical Hit|sw5e-phb|critical hit}; a natural 1 misses regardless of modifiers.
Ranged attacks with ship weapons have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} if you are within 50 feet of your target.

entries.name: Weapon Save DC
entries: Tertiary and quaternary weapons, and primary weapons on Huge and larger ships, often use a saving throw instead of an attack roll.
{@b Weapon save DC} = 8 + the crewmember's {@variantrule Proficiency|sw5e-phb|Proficiency Bonus} (if at least rank 1) + the ship's Wisdom modifier.

When an effect grants {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} or {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on an attack that uses a save instead of an attack roll, the save is made with advantage or disadvantage unless stated otherwise.
Add the ship's Strength modifier to damage from primary and secondary weapons.

variantrule.name: Patch
entries: When you take this action, you make a Constitution ({@skill Patch|sw5e-sotg}) check (DC = 10 or half the ship's missing hull points, whichever is higher) and expend one Hull Die to repair hull points. On a failure, you roll the Hull Die twice and take the lesser amount. On a success you roll the Hull Die normally. This action can be taken multiple times on a ship's turn.

variantrule.name: Ram
entries: When you take the Ram action, you make a Strength ({@skill Ram|sw5e-sotg}) check opposed by the target's Dexterity ({@skill Maneuvering|sw5e-sotg}) check. On a failure, the ram fails.
On a success, both ships take kinetic damage equal to two of your ship's Hull Dice + your ship's Strength modifier. If your ship has shield points remaining, your ship takes half this damage instead.
An Attack Run may allow a Ram with {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on the Ram check and bonus damage based on run distance (see the Helm action).

variantrule.name: Regenerate Shields
entries: When you take this action, you make a Strength ({@skill Boost|sw5e-sotg}) check (DC = 10 or half the ship's missing shield points, whichever is higher) and expend one shield die. On a failure, you roll the shield die twice and take the lesser amount. On a success you roll the shield die normally. This action can only be taken once each ship turn.

variantrule.name: Shield Points
entries: Many ships have shields—a buffer of energy measured in shield points in addition to hull points.
Whenever a ship with shield points takes damage, shields take the damage first. If damage reduces shield points to 0, the hull takes any remaining damage.

Shield point maximum and shield regeneration rate depend on shield dice, the ship's Strength modifier, and installed shield equipment (see {@book Chapter 5: Equipment|sw5e-sotg|7|Chapter 5: Equipment}).

variantrule.name: Ship Initiative
entries: Combat uses rounds and turns. During a round, each participant takes a turn; turn order is set by {@variantrule Initiative|sw5e-phb|initiative} at the start of the encounter.
Each PC on a ship rolls initiative normally. The {@b lowest} initiative among PCs on a ship sets that ship's initiative for the round.

On a ship's turn, the reactor replenishes power dice, the crew distributes them, and the crew may activate shield regeneration. All PCs on that ship then take individual turns in an order the crew agrees on (the helm breaks ties).

entries.name: NPC Ship Initiative
entries: For NPC ships, roll initiative as a Dexterity check modified by the ship's size:

variantrule.name: Space Versus Ground Scale
entries: Space combat uses scaled-down dice relative to ground combat. To convert between scales, multiply or divide damage, hull points, shield points, damage reduction, and shield regeneration by 10 as appropriate.

Large and larger ships may be immune to small-arms fire from individuals. Tiny starships are Tiny in space but Huge on the ground; Small ships are Gargantuan on the ground; Medium and larger ships are colossal.

Tiny–Large starships have {@variantrule Disadvantage|sw5e-phb|disadvantage} on attacks against Large or smaller creatures; those creatures have {@variantrule Advantage|sw5e-phb|advantage} on saves against such ships' weapons.

variantrule.name: Starship Damage Types
entries: Starship damage types differ slightly from ground combat. Notably, sonic damage does nothing in space.
{@b Acid}, {@b Cold}, and {@b Fire} deal half damage to shields.
{@b Energy} and {@b Force} deal normal damage to hull and shields.
{@b Ion} deals half damage to hull, cannot destroy ships outright—ion damage that would reduce a ship to 0 hull points instead leaves it {@condition Disabled|sw5e-sotg|disabled} and stable.
{@b Kinetic} deals normal damage; collisions deal kinetic damage.
{@b Lightning} deals half damage to hull.
{@b Necrotic} deals half damage to hull and shields.
{@b Poison} and {@b Psychic} deal no damage to ships.
{@b Sonic} deals normal damage in atmosphere but no damage in space.
{@b True} damage ignores effects that prevent or redirect damage.

entries.name: Starship Resistances and Immunities
entries: {@b Hull resistances:} Ion, Lightning, Necrotic. {@b Shield resistances:} Acid, Cold, Fire, Necrotic. {@b Hull and shield immunities:} Poison, Psychic.
